growth_stages.name: Germination
growth_stages.description: Seed imbibes water and radicle emerges.

growth_stages.name: Vegetative growth
growth_stages.description: Rapid leaf and stalk growth, highest nutrient demand.

growth_stages.name: Grain filling
growth_stages.description: Kernel development, milk to dough stage.

growth_stages.name: Physiological maturity
growth_stages.description: Black layer formation, ready for harvest.

operations.name: Land Clearing
operations.description: Removal of vegetation/debris from the plot.

operations.name: Pest & Disease Scouting/Control
operations.description: Fall armyworm and other pest management.

operations.name: Drying
operations.description: Field or platform drying to safe moisture content.

validation_rules.condition: Land preparation cannot be logged before land clearing, and should not be logged more than 30 days after it.
Planting cannot occur before land preparation is completed, and must occur within 14 days of it (soil loses tilth/moisture advantage after that).
Basal NPK (e.g. 15:15:15) should be applied at planting or within the first 1-2 weeks after planting.
validation_rules.source: IITA, Guide to Maize Production in Northern Nigeria, 2020; corroborated by Seed Co Nigeria agronomic guidance

validation_rules.condition: First manual weeding is recommended at 2 weeks after planting (earlier, from 2-3 weeks, if Imperata cylindrica is a problem).
validation_rules.source: Farmwarehouse / IITA extension guidance, Step by Step Maize Production in Nigeria

validation_rules.condition: Base/umbrella window (21-35 days) covering all regions in this file. The precise window differs by zone -- see regional_overrides: Guinea savanna is 28-35 days, Sudan savanna (extra-early varieties) is 21-28 days. Engines should apply the regional_overrides patch for maize_r5 when the farm's region is known, and fall back to this wider umbrella only when region is unknown.
validation_rules.source: IITA, Guide to Maize Production in Northern Nigeria, 2020

validation_rules.condition: Second manual weeding is recommended 4-5 weeks after planting.
validation_rules.source: Farmwarehouse / IITA extension guidance, Step by Step Maize Production in Nigeria

validation_rules.condition: Fall Armyworm control is most effective when insecticide is applied weekly during the first 3 weeks after planting; scouting/control logged well outside this window is flagged since FAW damage compounds quickly if missed early.
validation_rules.source: Farmwarehouse, Step by Step Maize Production in Nigeria (Ampligo/Emacot application schedule)

validation_rules.condition: Harvest cannot be logged before 80 days after planting (physiologically impossible even for the earliest-maturing hybrids) or after 150 days (implausible for all but the latest-maturing varieties; almost certainly a data error at this range).
validation_rules.source: Cross-referenced: Ghana MOFA Maize Production Guide (90-115 days), IITA/USAID Nigeria manuals (early/medium/late maturity classes), FAO regional guide (130-160 days for late varieties, though this is unusually long and treated as an upper bound rather than the norm)

validation_rules.condition: 90-120 days covers the typical medium-maturity hybrid grown across Nigerian Guinea/Sudan savanna zones. Harvest logged inside the hard block range (80-150 days) but outside this typical window is flagged so the farmer can confirm their variety's maturity class rather than being blocked outright.
validation_rules.source: IITA maturity-class guidance, cross-checked against Ghana MOFA (90-115 days)

validation_rules.condition: Harvest can only be logged once per planting cycle for an annual crop; a second harvest record requires a new planting record first.

Drying should begin promptly after harvest to bring grain to a safe storage moisture content and avoid mold/storage pest (grain weevil) infestation; the field-drying/harvest guidance from Feed the Future's manual notes maize is typically harvested close to physiological maturity and then requires deliberate drying, not left to dry indefinitely on the stalk.
validation_rules.source: IITA, Guide to Maize Production in Northern Nigeria, 2020 (storage pest section); Feed the Future Manual for Maize Farming

validation_rules.condition: Global rule: no operation may be logged with a date earlier than the previous operation's logged date for the same farm/cycle (no backdating that would reorder the sequence).

weather_preferences.notes: Sensitive to moisture stress during tasseling/silking; waterlogging is harmful at all stages.

diseases.name: Maize Streak Virus
diseases.symptoms: Chlorotic streaking along leaf veins, stunted growth.
diseases.management: Use resistant/tolerant varieties (e.g. ZPBSR, DMR-LSRW streak-resistant hybrids), control leafhopper vectors, plant early with the onset of rains.
diseases.source: IITA / USAID, Growing Maize in Nigeria

diseases.name: Maize Leaf Blight
diseases.management: Crop rotation, resistant varieties, fungicide if severe.
diseases.source: General extension guidance - less specifically documented in the Nigeria-specific sources reviewed so far; flagged for agronomist follow-up

pests.name: Fall Armyworm (FAW)
pests.symptoms: Ragged leaf feeding, sawdust-like frass in the whorl; larvae light green to dark brown with longitudinal stripes.
pests.management: Scout from emergence; approved insecticides (e.g. Ampligo, Emacot) applied once per week for the first 3 weeks after planting are effective in Nigeria. FAW affects 350+ plant species and is one of the most destructive invasive pests in the region.
pests.source: IITA, Guide to Maize Production in Northern Nigeria, 2020; Farmwarehouse, Step by Step Maize Production in Nigeria

pests.name: Striga (Striga hermonthica)
pests.symptoms: Parasitic weed attaching to maize roots; visible purple-flowered weed emergence, severe stunting and yield loss even before the weed itself is visible above ground.
pests.management: Resistant/tolerant hybrids, crop rotation with non-host (trap) crops, balanced soil fertility (Striga is worse on depleted soils), timely weeding before Striga seed-set.
pests.source: IITA, Guide to Maize Production in Northern Nigeria, 2020 - noted as a major constraint (up to 74% infestation in the northern Guinea savanna, 30-60% of yield losses attributed to it)

pests.name: Stem Borer
pests.symptoms: Bore holes in stalk, dead heart in young plants.
pests.management: Field sanitation, timely planting, targeted insecticide application.
pests.source: General extension guidance - not yet cross-checked against a Nigeria-specific primary source; flagged for agronomist follow-up

yield_model.notes: 1.2-2.0 t/ha reflects typical unoptimized smallholder yields; 2.5-3.5 t/ha (up to ~3+ t/ha) reflects recommended-practice yields in Northern Nigeria per IITA. Treat the top of this range as achievable-with-good-management rather than typical.

validation_rules.condition: Nitrogen top-dress (urea) applied 4-5 weeks after planting -- Guinea savanna zone window.
validation_rules.source: IITA, Guide to Maize Production in Northern Nigeria, 2020

validation_rules.condition: Nitrogen top-dress (urea) applied 3-4 weeks after planting for extra-early varieties -- Sudan savanna zone window (shorter than Guinea savanna because extra-early varieties are typically grown here).
validation_rules.source: IITA, Guide to Maize Production in Northern Nigeria, 2020

version_history.summary: Initial structured template built from general agronomic references. NOT yet validated by an agronomist - treat all intervals/thresholds as provisional.
version_history.source: Draft / general references (FAO, IITA public guidance) - pending expert review

version_history.changed_by: AgTrail Knowledge Base - sourced revision pass
version_history.summary: Replaced provisional intervals with numbers cross-checked against named published sources: fertilizer timing (basal 0-14 days, top-dress 21-35 days after planting), weeding schedule (14-21 and 28-35 days), Fall Armyworm spray window (0-21 days), and harvest window split into a hard block range (80-150 days, covering all maturity classes) plus a narrower warning range (90-120 days, typical medium-maturity varieties). Added Striga as a pest entry per IITA's emphasis on it as a major constraint. Every validation_rule and diseases/pests entry now carries a 'source' field. This is still NOT a substitute for an agronomist's sign-off -- it is a materially stronger draft, not a validated final version. Two entries (Maize Leaf Blight, Stem Borer) are explicitly flagged as weaker sources needing follow-up.
version_history.source: IITA - Guide to Maize Production in Northern Nigeria (2020); IITA/USAID - Growing Maize in Nigeria; Farmwarehouse - Step by Step Maize Production in Nigeria; Seed Co Nigeria - Good Agronomic Practices for Maize Farming; Ghana MOFA - Guide to Maize Production; Feed the Future Innovation Lab - Manual for Maize Farming

version_history.summary: Split the second_fertilizer (top-dress) timing rule by region rather than leaving one merged 21-35 day window: IITA's source actually gives Guinea savanna zones 28-35 days and Sudan savanna (extra-early varieties) 21-28 days -- these had been incorrectly averaged into a single range in v1.1.0. Base rule maize_r5 is now documented as a fallback umbrella for when region is unknown; regional_overrides carries the precise per-zone window. This is the first crop file to actually use regional_overrides, so it also establishes the convention: overrides.validation_rules is a list of partial patches keyed by rule_id, applied over the base rule of the same id.
version_history.source: IITA, Guide to Maize Production in Northern Nigeria, 2020
